Aria is a dependency-free native runtime that runs the complete text-to-music pipeline of Stable Audio 3 (SA3) on ordinary GPUs, CPU-only machines, and a Raspberry Pi 5, with no Python or deep-learning framework underneath.
Eight-bit precision in the aria runtime shows no measurable quality loss on prompt adherence, overall audio quality, and taste preservation while sharply cutting memory usage.
Four-bit precision in the aria runtime adds a small, bounded cost but allows the 1.2-billion-parameter model to run on an 8 GB Raspberry Pi.
Aria matches or exceeds the generation speed of the official Stable Audio 3 implementation and starts about seven times faster.
The aria runtime exposes activation steering, a low-cost way to steer what the model generates, enabling music with taste associations (sonic seasoning).
